## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

data.description:
Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Scaffold hook wiring, thresholds and full-suite hook (merged 1+2+3)

Implementation slice for **AC1** of `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`, merging the plan's
test-first child (`CG-0MW0SBXKW000T4C0`) with the two implementation children
`CG-0MW0SC4LO0097JMV` (hook wiring) and `CG-0MW0SC46S007E6GC` (thresholds).

**Why merged (recorded decision, 2026-11-03):** the plan's child 1 delivered
*only* failing-first assertions ("no production code changes"), but the
implement workflow's `finish` gate requires the changed-scope suite to be
green. A deliberately-red-only item can therefore never reach `in_review`.
All three scopes are one vertical slice over the same file
(`scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) and the same test file, so they are delivered
together, tests first within the worktree (red → green before commit).

## Goal

A freshly scaffolded `tce-<game>` repo comes out with **active** git hooks
(`core.hooksPath=.githooks`), the **unified full-suite** `pre-push` hook, and a
committed, measured `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` plus the refresh
entry point — no manual per-clone activation, no gate-less v2 hook, and a
fail-closed (not silently fail-open) context-budget gate from day one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hooks copied from the core (single source of truth).**
  `scaffoldGameRepo()` copies every file from `<coreRoot>/.githooks/` into
  `<gameRepoRoot>/.githooks/` byte-identically, preserving the executable bit;
  no hook content is forked into a template string in the scaffold.
- **AC2 — `core.hooksPath` wired.** After a non-dry, non-selection run in a git
  repo, `git -C <gameRepoRoot> config core.hooksPath` is `.githooks` and
  `git -C <gameRepoRoot> rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves inside
  `<gameRepoRoot>/.githooks`. A dry run or `--only` run configures nothing. A
  target that is not a git repo is skipped with an explicit report entry (never
  a throw), so the scaffold keeps working on a pre-`git init` tree.
- **AC3 — Unified full-suite hook content.** The core `.githooks/pre-push` is
  upgraded to the unified **v3** variant: it keeps the existing branch policy,
  context-budget and worklog-sync gates and adds the full-suite test gate for
  `refs/heads/dev|main` with the runner resolved **local → global**
  (`<repo>/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, then
  `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), failing closed with a
  message naming `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (and `install_pi.sh` when neither runner
  exists). No existing gate or bypass variable is weakened.
- **AC4 — Thresholds generated from the measured surface.** After a non-dry
  run, `<gameRepoRoot>/docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` carries the
  per-component measured byte values (`global_agents`, `project_agents`,
  `skills_prose`, `total`) for the **game repo** root, produced by
  `measure_context.py --repo-root <gameRepoRoot> --include-hidden
  --generate-thresholds`; it immediately passes the structured validation.
  Resolution is local-then-global (`<coreRoot>/skill/context-audit/...`, then
  `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/...`). When `python3` or the script is
  unavailable the scaffold writes **no** guessed file, records a report entry
  naming the remedy, and stays fail-open — never throws.
- **AC5 — Refresh entry point + generated guidance.** `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`
  is copied from the core into the generated repo (resolving `REPO_ROOT` to the
  game repo, not `core/`), and a short generated `docs/dev/context-budget.md`
  note documents activation, refresh and the one-activation-step-on-fresh-clone
  caveat.
- **AC6 — Plan/report contract preserved.** Every new file rides the existing
  `classifyAndApply` machinery: `create` on a fresh tree, `unchanged` on an
  immediate re-scaffold, `skip-local` when diverged and no `--force`, nothing
  written by `--dry-run` (whose report still classifies). `ScaffoldResult`
  reports the hooks-path wiring outcome and the thresholds outcome, and the CLI
  prints both.
- **AC7 — Tests.** `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` covers every
  assertion above (git-verified hooks path + hooks-dir resolution, byte-identical
  hook parity, v3 gate markers, thresholds validity, non-git tolerance, dry run,
  idempotence, selection mode, report classification) and is green.

## Deliverables

- `.githooks/pre-push` — unified v3 hook in TCE (source of truth copied into
  generated repos).
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — hook copy + `core.hooksPath` wiring +
  thresholds/refresh/doc generation + report fields.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — assertions above.

## Key Files

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
- `.githooks/pre-push`
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` (copied source)
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (reference for the generated note)

## Notes

- Framework hook content / `install_pi.sh` remain owned by
  `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (SorraAgents); this item only aligns TCE's committed
  hook with the unified v3 design so the scaffold can copy it verbatim.
- `--strict-git-env` already exempts a git-exported worktree-managed `GIT_DIR`
  in the shared runner (`git_sandbox.repository_override_vars_present`), so the
  worktree push path needs verification, not a hook change (child
  `CG-0MW0SC8A2003UEX6`).
data.title: Scaffold hook wiring, thresholds and unified v3 pre-push hook (merged 1+2+3)

# Linked-worktree push gating end-to-end test

Verification slice for AC2 of `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`: prove the gate actually runs
(and actually blocks) when pushing from a **linked worktree** of a scaffolded
repo — the case where a naive `GIT_DIR` strictness check or a `--show-toplevel`
assumption can silently disable hooks.

## Goal

An end-to-end test that scaffolds a temp repo into a bare-remote-backed
configuration, creates a linked worktree, pushes a `dev` branch from it with a
stub test runner on `PATH`, and asserts both that the runner was invoked and that
a red suite **blocks** the push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Runner invoked from a linked worktree.** With a stub `run_tests.py`
  (or `TEST_RUNNER` override the hook honours) that records its invocation to a
  file and exits 0, a push from a linked worktree succeeds and the stub's marker
  file exists. No `--strict-git-env` refusal appears in the output.
- **AC2 — Red suite gates the push.** With the stub exiting non-zero, the same
  worktree push fails with a non-zero git exit, the branch is **not** advanced on
  the bare remote, and the hook's failure message names the remedy.
- **AC3 — Linked-worktree `GIT_DIR` exempt.** The test covers the documented
  exemption for a worktree-managed `GIT_DIR` (`docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9):
  wherever the hook validates the git environment, `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`
  / per-worktree `git-dir` are treated as legitimate, so a real worktree push is
  never refused as if it were an exported `GIT_DIR`.
- **AC4 — No global state leakage.** The test uses temp dirs, a `file://` bare
  remote, a stub runner and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=0`; it never invokes the real suite,
  never touches the developer's hooks or config, and is safe to run in CI.
- **AC5 — Bounded runtime.** The test completes in well under a minute (stub
  runner only; no `npm install`, no Phaser/browser work).

## Minimal implementation

- `git init --bare` a temp remote; `git init` + commit a minimal tree; run
  `scaffoldGameRepo()` to wire hooks; `git worktree add` a linked worktree; push
  from it to the bare remote with a `PATH`-prepended stub runner dir.
- Assert on git exit codes, the stub marker, and the absent remote ref.
- Reuse the fixture helpers from the test-first item so both items share the
  temp-repo setup instead of duplicating it.

- **Parent AC2 coverage.** Covers parent AC2 — Worktree-safe under `--strict-git-env`: a push from a linked worktree of a scaffolded repo runs the gate and is gated, with no `--strict-git-env` refusal; the end-to-end test pushes from a linked worktree with a stub runner and asserts the suite is invoked and the push is gated (git-exported worktree-managed `GIT_DIR` exempt).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the hook-wiring implementation item (hooks must be active first).
- Blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` for the unified hook's strict-env/worktree
  behaviour; if that item's hook refuses worktree pushes, this test surfaces it
  there rather than being worked around here.

## Deliverables

- New worktree-push test coverage (file named for the behaviour, e.g.
  `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.hook-gate.test.ts` or a dedicated describe
  block in the existing scaffold suite).

## Key Files

- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — shared fixtures.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — the gate under test.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9 — the `GIT_DIR` exemption contract.
data.title: Linked-worktree push gating end-to-end test

# Roll out full-suite gate to tce-main-street

Rollout slice for AC3/AC5 of `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`: prove the scaffold wiring on a
real consumer repo (`../tce-main-street`) and record the gate-produced cache
entry as evidence.

## Goal

`../tce-main-street` ends with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, the unified full-suite
pre-push hook, a committed `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, and one real
`dev` push that was gated by the full suite and populated a cache entry the audit
skill can use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Wiring applied to the real repo.** Running the scaffold against
  `../tce-main-street` (never editing SorraAgents) leaves `git config
  core.hooksPath` = `.githooks`, `.githooks/pre-push` byte-identical to the core's
  unified variant, and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` committed and
  passing `--check`. No unversioned `.git/hooks/pre-push` copy remains in use.
- **AC2 — Real gated `dev` push.** A `dev` push from `../tce-main-street` runs the
  full suite through the hook and succeeds; the run leaves a full-suite cache
  entry at that repo's git state (queryable via the test skill's cache).
- **AC3 — Evidence recorded.** The push output (or a captured log) plus the cache
  entry key are recorded as a comment on `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`, together with the
  exact commands used and the hook version marker observed.
- **AC4 — Game-repo tests still green.** The game repo's own suite passes after
  the wiring (run via the test skill; a hook that blocks every game push would be
  a release blocker), and the cross-repo change is pushed to `dev` only.
- **AC5 — Full engine suite green.** The engine full suite passes at the final
  commit (run via `/skill:test`), which satisfies AC5 of the parent item, and the
  green run is what the audit consumes.

## Minimal implementation

- Run the scaffold in non-dry mode against the sibling checkout, inspect the
  classification report, and commit only the generated/expected files in the game
  repo (its own Worklog store records the change).
- Perform one real `dev` push from a work-item branch merge path and capture the
  hook output.
- If the full-suite gate is prohibitively slow for the first rollout, capture the
  timing and note it on the parent item rather than bypassing the gate.

- **Parent AC3 + AC5 coverage.** Covers parent AC3 — Rollout verified in a real game repo and documented: re-run the scaffold/installer against `../tce-main-street`, confirm `core.hooksPath` and the full-suite gate on a real `dev` push (a gate-produced full-suite cache entry exists), and record rollout evidence on the parent item. Also covers parent AC5 — Tests green: the full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the hook-wiring, thresholds and linked-worktree test items.
- Blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`.

## Deliverables

- Wired `../tce-main-street` checkout (committed + pushed to its `dev`).
- Evidence comment on the parent item (commands, log excerpt, cache key).

## Key Files

- `../tce-main-street/.githooks/pre-push` — installed unified hook.
- `../tce-main-street/docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — generated budget.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the tool that applies the wiring.
data.title: Roll out full-suite gate to tce-main-street

# Document scaffold hook activation and thresholds

Documentation slice for AC4 of `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`: the scaffold/hook behaviour
change must be documented in the same commits as the code, per the project
doc-update policy.

## Goal

A developer reading `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` or `docs/dev/context-budget.md`
learns what a scaffolded game repo now gets (active hooks, full-suite gate,
seeded thresholds), how to refresh thresholds, and the one activation step a
fresh clone still needs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Scaffold docs updated.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md`'s scaffold section states
  that a scaffold wires `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, copies `.githooks/` from the
  core, emits the unified full-suite pre-push hook and seeds
  `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, and names the write-classification
  behaviour (`--only` / `--force` / `--dry-run`) for the new entries.
- **AC2 — Context-budget doc covers game repos.** TCE's `docs/dev/context-budget.md`
  gains a section on scaffolded game repos: threshold generation at scaffold
  time, the `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh --check` workflow inside a
  game repo, and the fail-open/fail-closed split.
- **AC3 — One activation step documented.** The fresh-clone caveat is stated
  explicitly wherever activation is described: `core.hooksPath` is **local**
  config, so a clone needs `install_pi.sh` or
  `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once (with the reason, not just the
  command).
- **AC4 — Stale claims removed.** Every statement that game repos cannot have
  the full-suite gate (or that only TCE gets it) is removed or corrected; a grep
  for the old wording returns nothing.
- **AC5 — README pointer.** `README.md` mentions the gate for game repos
  (one short paragraph or bullet) and links to the developer docs section.
- **AC6 — Code comments.** Non-obvious scaffold additions carry comments naming
  the source of truth (the core `.githooks/` copy) and the fail-open rationale
  for missing measurement tooling.

## Minimal implementation

- Edit the three docs in the same commit as the corresponding code change where
  practical; otherwise create this item as a child kept open until closed.
- Keep the wording UK English and consistent with the existing tables.

- **Parent AC4 coverage.** Covers parent AC4 — Documentation: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and the TCE-owned `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (scaffold activation, threshold generation, the one-activation-step-on-fresh-clone caveat); stale claims that game repos cannot have the gate are removed.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the hook-wiring and thresholds implementation items (docs describe
  settled behaviour, not intentions).

## Deliverables

- Updated `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md`,
  plus code comments.

## Key Files

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — scaffold + hooks section.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — game-repo section and activation caveat.
- `README.md` — quality-gates pointer.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — code comments.
data.title: Document scaffold hook activation and thresholds
